item.title: Most in US prefer big houses, even if community is farther away | Pew Research Center
item.description: 55% of Americans say they would prefer to live in a community where houses are larger and farther away from amenities – compared to 44% who say the opposite.

item.title: Key findings about Black immigrants in the US | Pew Research Center
item.description: The U.S. Black immigrant population has more than doubled since 2000, reaching 5.6 million in 2024 and now making up 11.4% of the total Black population.

item.title: Most Americans say medical aid in dying is morally permissible | Pew Research Center
item.description: Republicans are twice as likely as Democrats to call physician-assisted death morally wrong (48% vs. 23%).

item.title: 1 in 4 US Radio Stations Are Religious, Reaching Nearly All Americans | Pew Research Center
item.description: Almost all U.S. adults live in range of a religious radio station, most commonly Christian radio. Stations tend to broadcast either mostly music or mostly talk.

item.title: Who listens to religious audio programming in the US? | Pew Research Center
item.description: About this research This Pew Research Center report from the Pew-Knight Initiative is about the AM and FM radio stations across the United States that primarily broadcast religious or faith-based…

item.title: How Catholic radio differs from other Christian radio | Pew Research Center
item.description: Catholic radio features more talk programming and distinct topics compared with other Christian stations. Explore how it stands out in the U.S. media landscape.

item.title: Political commentary on religious radio: what listeners think | Pew Research Center
item.description: Most religious radio listeners say keeping up with news and politics isn't a major reason they tune in. Still, some stations have a heavy focus on political commentary.

item.title: Music on religious radio: artists, genres and listeners | Pew Research Center
item.description: Music fills half of religious radio airtime in the U.S. Most songs played fall in the contemporary Christian or worship genres, and a handful of artists dominate airwaves.

item.title: Religious radio stations: location, ownership and reach | Pew Research Center
item.description: More than 4,000 religious AM/FM stations broadcast across the U.S. Read about where they are, what their range looks like and independent versus group ownership.

item.title: Religious radio stations in each US state | Pew Research Center
item.description: Explore each state's population of religious radio stations and how their programming differs.

item.title: Many Latin Americans see a role for religion in government, national identity | Pew Research Center
item.description: Majorities in Brazil, Colombia and Peru want leaders who stand up for their religious beliefs. Protestants are especially supportive of Christianity in public life.

item.title: About 9% of U.S. births in 2023 were to unauthorized or temporary legal immigrant mothers | Pew Research Center
item.description: Generally, the trends in births to unauthorized immigrants follow the growth and decline of the unauthorized immigrant population.

item.title: Birthright citizenship is not common in countries outside the US | Pew Research Center
item.description: 32 other countries around the world have birthright citizenship laws that are substantially similar to the U.S. Another 50 or so countries have more limited variations of birthright citizenship.
